papers.title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
papers.authors: Huang A, He J, Ying GS, Binenbaum G, Abbasian J, Oatts JT.
papers.abstract: Objective or purpose To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children. Design Retrospective cohort study. Participants Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded. Methods Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use. Main outcome measures Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Results Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension. Conclusions Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.

papers.title: G-quadruplex profiling using single-cell CUT&Tag offers insight into the epigenetic landscape of the developing mouse brain.
papers.authors: Lyu J, Hetey S, Öztürk MA, Castelo-Branco G, Bartosovic M, Elsässer SJ.
papers.abstract: Background G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical DNA structures that have gained increasing attention for their potential roles in gene regulation and role in neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. Despite their biological significance, G4 structures have not been studied systematically across tissues and cell types. Results In this study, we employ G4 single-cell CUT&Tag (G4 scCUT&Tag) to characterize G4 landscapes in postnatal mouse brain cells, leveraging single-cell analytical approaches commonly used in scRNA-Seq and scATAC-Seq datasets. Using conventional single-cell omics workflows to process and explore our data, we distinguish distinct cell lineages based on G4 heterogeneity and establish that a subset of lineage-specific genes show unique promoter G4s. Multi-omics integration with scRNA-Seq gene expression profiles, using both a covariance-based technique (canonical correlation analysis) and a transfer learning-based approach, enables more accurate cell-type annotation. These integrations not only reveal correlations between G4 signal and gene expression, but demonstrate that G4 scCUT&Tag enables detailed examination of G4 heterogeneity in complex tissues and supports integrative analysis of G4 profiles with other omics layers, offering new insights into the epigenomic landscapes of the developing brain. Conclusions Our findings establish G4 scCUT&Tag as a framework for investigating the cellular heterogeneity of G4 landscapes in complex tissues and provide a basis for exploring their relationships with gene regulation and other layers of chromatin organization.

papers.title: Single-nucleus multiomic profiling uncovers epigenetic dysregulation driving hippocampal vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Tao Q, Luo T, Wang P, Jiang M, Lai Z, Jin B, Liu Y, He Y, Wei Y, Gao Y, Zhu L, Du H, Wang L, Peng Y, Hou Y, Liu S, Liu L, Zhang J, Han L.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits region- and cell-type-specific vulnerability, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. We performed integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq of human hippocampus to resolve gene regulatory architecture in AD. By linking chromatin accessibility to transcription, we identified more than 1000 disease-associated cis-regulatory interactions, highlighting coordinated epigenomic-transcriptomic remodeling. Excitatory cornu ammonis (EX.CA) neurons exhibited disproportionate regulatory disruption, characterized by increased chromatin accessibility coupled to activation of apoptosis-related gene programs, whereas dentate gyrus (EX.DG) neurons remained comparatively resistant. In glial cells, regulatory network inference revealed activation of transcription factor modules centered on SPI1/KLF4 in microglia and STAT3 in astrocytes, defining epigenetic programs that are highly associated with inflammatory and metabolic state transitions. Comparative evaluation with the prefrontal cortex uncovered conserved inflammatory activation alongside region-specific immune regulatory divergence, indicating spatially distinct microglial responses. Furthermore, cross-species integration demonstrated that a substantial fraction of AD-associated regulatory elements are human-specific, with AD-risk variants enriched in microglial cis-regulatory elements at loci including BIN1 and APOE . Together, these results provide a mechanistic framework linking chromatin remodeling to cell-type-specific dysfunction and reveal human-specific regulatory architecture as a crucial factor to AD vulnerability and translational limitation.

papers.title: Implications of Image-Level Duplication in Public Glaucoma Datasets.
papers.authors: Endo I, Fukuhara Y, Oka S.
papers.abstract: Importance Medical artificial intelligence (AI) can be trusted only if validated in patients not used for development. In glaucoma AI, a few public datasets from 1 laboratory serve as those independent cohorts. Objective To determine whether 3 public glaucoma datasets used for external validation and fairness evaluation are independent patient cohorts. Design, setting, and participants This cross-sectional dataset audit and record-linkage analysis was conducted in July 2026 using the publicly distributed files of Harvard-GDP (1000 eyes), Harvard-GF (3300 eyes), and Harvard-FairVision (10 000 eyes), all from a single laboratory. Records were linked by exact visual field and demographic fingerprints, with chance modeled from the within-dataset collision rate and permutation. All 1302 candidate pairs underwent direct image comparison. Main outcomes and measures Number of shared eyes and image-level identity of optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans distributed under different identifiers. Results Harvard-GF and Harvard-FairVision matched on 1302 eyes against 1.9 expected by chance. Direct comparison confirmed 1031 (79.2%; 95% CI, 76.9%-81.4%) as the same 3-dimensional OCT volume (cosine similarity ≥0.9999; 88% of voxels exactly equal), at least 31% of the 3300 Harvard-GF eyes, a lower bound. Duplication was similar across the 3 Harvard-FairVision splits (78.5%-80.8%). Harvard-GDP and Harvard-GF shared 22 eyes matching exactly on all 52 total-deviation points and mean deviation, all in the Harvard-GF validation split; Harvard-GDP distributes no OCT volume, so its overlap rests on weaker evidence. No file carried a patient identifier, and no release disclosed the overlap; among the 64 of 105 citing studies whose full text we obtained, none reported it. Across 5 training runs, a classifier trained on 1 dataset and evaluated on the other gave an area under the curve of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) where 78.5% (95% CI, 74.0%-82.5%) of test eyes were training data, against 0.78 (95% CI, 0.72-0.83) out of sample (inflation, 0.12; 95% CI, 0.06-0.18). Inflation occurred in every racial subgroup and was larger where out-of-sample performance was lower (Spearman ρ = -0.57; permutation P = .02). Conclusions and relevance These findings suggest that the examined datasets were not independent cohorts. Treating them as independent benchmarks inflates reported performance and might mask fairness gaps through data leakage and nonindependent validation.

papers.title: The ONSET Study: Optic Neuritis Frequently Represents the Onset of Central Nervous System Inflammatory Disease.
papers.authors: Mori S, Ueki S, Maekubo T, Nakano E, Chuman H, Mochizuki Y, Himori N, Mori S, Matsumoto T, Yasuda S, Hanai K, ONSET Study Group.
papers.abstract: Purpose To determine the long-term diagnostic transition and temporal pattern of central nervous system (CNS) inflammatory events after a first episode of optic neuritis. Design Multicenter retrospective cohort study. Subjects Six hundred one consecutive patients with first-episode optic neuritis who presented to 11 tertiary referral centers in Japan between January 2016 and December 2023. Methods Patients with MRI-confirmed first-episode optic neuritis were retrospectively enrolled. Clinical characteristics, antibody status, treatments, subsequent events, and final diagnoses were collected from longitudinal follow-up. Main outcome measures Transition in the diagnosis of optic neuritis from the time of initial onset to the end of longitudinal follow-up. Results A total of 601 patients were enrolled and followed for a median of 2 years (interquartile range [IQR], 1-4.5 years). At onset, initial diagnoses were idiopathic in 295 patients (49.1%), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) in 134 (22.3%), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in 120 (20.0%), multiple sclerosis (MS) in 16 (2.7%), and other diagnoses in 36 (6.0%). At last follow-up, final diagnoses were single isolated optic neuritis in 222 patients (36.9%), recurrent isolated optic neuritis in 23 (3.8%), MOGAD in 134 (22.3%), NMOSD in 125 (20.8%), MS in 77 (12.8%), and other diagnoses in 20 (3.3%). Overall, 166 of 601 patients (27.6%) experienced at least one CNS inflammatory event other than the initial optic neuritis. Recurrent optic neuritis was the most frequent event (58.8%), followed by encephalitis (22.9%) and myelitis (18.3%). Among patients with post-onset events, 64 (48.9%) developed an event within 1 year and 97 (74.0%) within 2 years after the initial episode of optic neuritis. Among the 131 patients with post-onset events, more than half (77 patients, 58.8%) developed outside maintenance therapy, including 68 after treatment discontinuation and 9 without maintenance therapy. Conclusions More than one-quarter of patients with first-episode optic neuritis experienced CNS inflammatory events other than the initial optic neuritis, and only approximately one-third ultimately remained classified as having single isolated optic neuritis. These findings demonstrate that first-episode optic neuritis frequently represents the onset of an underlying CNS inflammatory disease, underscoring the importance of long-term neurological surveillance following the initial episode.

papers.title: Step change in glaucoma polygenic risk score performance enables clinical utility.
papers.authors: MacGregor S, Ni G, Seviiri M, Kolovos A, Le NQ, Hassall MM, Schmidt J, Gharahkhani P, Tang V, Souzeau E, Qassim A, Nandakumar P, Shringarpure S, Granka JM, Cooke Bailey JN, Aung T, Landers J, Graham SL, Healey PR, Khawaja AP, Pasquale LR, Wiggs JL, O'Brien J, Weinreb RN, Willoughby CE, Lotery A, Mitchell P, Mackey DA, Hewitt AW, Haan N, Siggs OM, Craig JE.
papers.abstract: Purpose Open-angle glaucoma (OAG) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness and is highly heritable. Despite effective treatments, approximately 50% of cases remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate a clinically applicable, genetics-based risk prediction tool for OAG across diverse ancestries. Design Genetic association study and risk prediction analysis. Participants More than 6 million individuals contributing genome-wide association study data from multiple ancestry groups. Methods We constructed a comprehensive polygenic risk score (PRS) for OAG using a multitrait modeling framework that integrated glaucoma-related traits, including intraocular pressure, optic disc parameters, and ocular hypertension. PRS performance was evaluated for OAG risk across major ancestry groups and assessed for associations with age at diagnosis, treatment escalation, surgical outcomes, and familial risk. Main outcome measures Odds ratios (ORs) for OAG by PRS percentile, age at disease onset, absolute risk estimates, treatment escalation, glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk in first-degree relatives. Results In Australian individuals of European ancestry, those in the top 10% of the PRS distribution had a 10-fold increased risk of OAG compared with the remainder (OR 10.04, 95% CI 7.43-13.59), substantially outperforming our previously published PRS (OR 4.2). Similar performance was observed in U.S. European ancestry data (OR 9.09, 95% CI 5.09-16.26). In UK Biobank Europeans the OR for the top 10% versus the remainder was 4.91 (95% CI 4.25-5.69). Although performance was attenuated in other ancestry groups (OR top 10% vs. remainder: 4.01 in South Asian, 3.39 in East Asian, and ranging from 2.26 to 3.81 in African ancestry populations depending on cohort), high PRS percentiles corresponded to elevated absolute risk across all groups. On average, individuals in the highest-risk decile developed glaucoma approximately 25 years earlier than those in the lowest decile and had ∼100-fold (OR 96.83, 95% CI 52.61-178.21) higher risk. The PRS also predicted treatment escalation in early disease, prevalent and incident glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk among first-degree relatives. Conclusions This enhanced PRS, available for clinical use through an accredited genotyping workflow, enables effective risk stratification for OAG across diverse ancestries, facilitating earlier identification and treatment of high-risk individuals while supporting resource rationalisation for those at low risk. Performance is strongest in European ancestry populations, and further work is needed to improve equity of performance across ancestries.

papers.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Nie H, Dai Z, Zhao L, Wan Y, Wang Y, Chen Y, Chen X, Xu Z, Zhong J, Cheng D, Wu Q, Ouyang C, Lin P, Deng H, Liu Z, Li G, Yin C, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)-like immune architectures in mismatch repair-deficient tumors associated with response to anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T-dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ-dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes.
papers.authors: Cai W, Wang Y, Huang F, Zhang Y, Gu M, Yang C, Li P, Jiang W, Yang X, Xu X, Li X, Ma D, Xia F, Xu Z, Liu Y, Spruill V, Guo J, Xu S, Wang Y, Krishnan Y, Qiu L, Hu M, Xu H.
papers.abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging-based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

papers.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.
papers.authors: Xue F, Zhao S, Tian H, Li L, Xu X, Lu Y, Xu K, He L, Wang Y, Ba Z, Que Y, Liu D, Xing Y, Su Y, Xing M, Zeng W.
papers.abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

papers.title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity.
papers.authors: dePolo DL, Yuan T, King MA, Zhong S.
papers.abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth's viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

papers.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space.
papers.authors: Su B, Rockström J, Chen D, Fetzer I, Feng H, Hugelius G, Winkelmann R, Norström AV, Xiao C, Hanna E, Alverson K, Box JE, Qin D, Sommerkorn M, Andreassen LM, Heil P, Yao T, Richardson K, Lade SJ, Bai X, Gupta J, Stewart-Koster B, Zheng Z, Pomeroy J, Mackintosh A, Oki T, Mukherji A, Jackson M, Rocha JC, Donges JF, Wang-Erlandsson L.
papers.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

papers.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants.
papers.authors: Madsen AE, Pushpakumara TV, Weerathunga US, Weerakoon DK, de Silva S.
papers.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

papers.title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990.
papers.authors: Morgan EJ, Jin Y, Kozlova E, Watson AJ, Manning AC, Zaehle S, Tohjima Y, Lan X, Keeling RF.
papers.abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year -1 decade -1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year -1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year -1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

papers.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs.
papers.authors: Sadayappan K, Li L.
papers.abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

papers.abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

papers.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA).
papers.authors: Mazzone E, Marconato L, Fanelli A, Cascione L, Bertoni F, Marchiò C, Sapino A, Aresu L.
papers.abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

papers.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly.
papers.authors: Liu Q, Bai Z, Liu T, Jia F, Ji Y, Chen C, Gong Y, Duan L, Zhou J, Guo Q, Zhu L, Kang H, Wang H, Shen Z, Huang X, Shen J, Shao W, Chang J, Chai J, Zhang Y, Han Z, Zhang C, Hu Z.
papers.abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a "molecular glue," stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain-containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This "produce-and-trap" mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

papers.title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases.
papers.authors: Kim S, Cheong S, Lee S, Kim Y, Xie R, Koh IG, La J, Hwa C, An H, Park J, An JY, Wang B, Park JE.
papers.abstract: Diseases affect multiple cell types within tissues, but the overall landscape of the multicellular responses in human diseases remains largely unexplored. Here we categorize the multicellular responses of human diseases based on a remapped atlas of human cells, PANGEA, incorporating 12.6 million cells acquired from a pipeline that automatically processes raw sequence files from public repositories. We constructed a hierarchical cell classification framework comprising 32 major cell types and 165 cellular subtypes. On the basis of this annotation framework, we explored an extensive atlas of human cells containing 46.5 million cells from 160 diseases across 48 organs and revealed core archetypes of human diseases repeatedly found across organs. We show that this cell atlas could also serve as a reference for unbiased analysis in spatial transcriptomics, revealing spatial features associated with immunotherapy responses. Collectively, our study provides foundational resources for cell ontologies, enabling cross-tissue comparisons of cellular features in human diseases.

papers.authors: Kothandan SV, Siddiqui MG, Galor A, Basu S, Singh S.
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether individuals with Sjögren's disease (SjD) and light sensitivity differ in corneal nerve morphology, tear cytokines, or neuropeptide profiles from those with SjD without light sensitivity and with controls. Methods This pilot, cross-sectional study conducted at a tertiary eye hospital in India included SjD patients with (n=10, defined as a "yes" response to light-induced or light-exacerbated ocular pain) and without light sensitivity (n=10; satisfied ACR/EULAR 2016 criteria; not on topical antiinflammatory), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=9). Groups were compared for Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), tear film parameters, ocular surface staining, symptom-sign alignment, mechanical corneal sensitivity, in-vivo confocal microscopy, tear cytokines, and neuropeptides. Results The two SjD groups were similar with respect to demographics, OSDI scores (excluding light sensitivity item), tear film parameters, symptom-sign alignment, and corneal nerve metrics. However, SjD with light sensitivity exhibited reduced mechanical corneal sensitivity (38.5 ± 11.1 vs. 54 ± 2.1 mm; p = 0.0006), decreased mature dendritic cell density (3 ± 4 vs. 7.7 ± 4.6 cells/mm 2 ; p = 0.04), and lower levels of inflammatory cytokines (IL-17, IL-13, IL-10, and IL-5), compared with SjD without light sensitivity. Compared with controls, both SjD groups had significantly higher symptom severity, abnormal tear parameters, and a more inflammatory ocular surface profile. Conclusion The findings of reduced mechanical sensitivity and less ocular surface inflammation in the SjD with light sensitivity group suggest different SjD clinical phenotypes, potentially distinguishing those with a greater contribution of altered sensory processing from those with predominantly ocular surface-driven inflammatory disease.

papers.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
papers.authors: Okin D, Choi JH, Wang C, Cao A, Fisch D, Ma W, Lindblad KE, Valenti M, Kooistra T, Nguyen T, Hariri LP, Chaudhary N, Tien YC, Borges da Silva H, Knipe RS, Mbalaviele G, Kagan JC.
papers.abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity 1,2 . Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis 1,3 . By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone-osteoclasts-had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity.

papers.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores.
papers.authors: Yu M, Heidari M, Palacio-Rodriguez K, Ruan H, Mingu S, Chen Y, Gou XZ, Shen P, Liu S, Chen SY, Hidayat AA, Bode M, Sikora M, Tang AH, Hummer G, Lemke EA.
papers.abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm 1,2 . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated 3-13 . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG-FG and FG-importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations 14 of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization 4,5,7,9,15 and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

papers.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China.
papers.authors: Meng L, Yang H, Miller G, Li H.
papers.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline 1-10 . Notably, even China's total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China's one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China's total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research.

papers.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Tan J, Neba EC, Morival S, Frankowski K, Daval B, Viola IM.
papers.abstract: The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs 2,3 . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

papers.title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity.
papers.authors: Jackson TD, Palozzi JM, McGann CD, Vitale T, Choa R, Nguyen HHM, Paulo JA, Latorre-Muro P, Van Vranken JG, Ravichandran M, Zhang B, Yadav M, Gygi SP, Puigserver P.
papers.abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations 1 , including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8 + T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation 2 , suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

papers.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA.
papers.authors: Donaldson GP, Lima Dos Reis G, Saad M, Wichmann C, Mamede I, Chen G, Harrer CE, DelGaudio NL, Zhang D, Aydin B, Castro TBR, Grivennikov SI, Reis BS, Liu EG, Eisenbarth SC, Birsoy K, Tavazoie SF, Stadtmueller BM, Victora GD, Mucida D.
papers.abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis 1 . IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function 2,3 , with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities 4-8 . Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

papers.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti.
papers.authors: Pillet MD, Maitner BS, Arakaki M, Araujo DSA, Baker MA, Barrios D, Boyle BL, Breshears DD, Feng X, Goettsch B, Guerrero PC, Hernández-Hernández T, Majure LC, Meriño BM, Nikolopoulos EI, Puente-Martínez R, Roehrdanz PR, Serra-Diaz JM, Urban MC, Merow C, Enquist BJ.
papers.abstract: Extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change 1 . Their effects on species' distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood 2-9 . Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought 10 , including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family 11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58-61% to 69-72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26-43% to 55-58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1-15% to 25-35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69-72% to 84-85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

papers.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart.
papers.authors: Polo Rivera C, Roske JJ, Hands EL, Fassetta F, Sale JE, Yeeles JTP.
papers.abstract: Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45-MCM-GINS) helicase 1,2 . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability 3-6 . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment 4 . In human cells, the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress 7-10 , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A 9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG-PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

papers.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis.
papers.authors: Furth N, Riemenschneider C, Arieli Y, Avni M, Povolotski MY, Yung H, Karagach S, Atrakchi O, Erez N, Salame TM, Noberini R, Durand A, Jouault G, Dassa B, Zerbib M, Oren R, Golani O, Bar-Zakai B, Mavor Y, Friedman-Eldar O, Kadar-Sfarad H, Gilron S, Givon-Madhala O, Ronel N, Abu-Rmilah F, Moshe I, Ish-Shalom S, Yosepovich A, Kaplan M, Bakalenik M, Dadiani M, Tryggvadottir R, Shatkin G, Hakobyan M, Kovacsovics A, Mackowiak SD, Arnold A, McLaughlin S, Andreishcheva E, Shinde A, Zhang J, Jones D, Nili Gal-Yam E, Geiger T, Bonaldi T, Feinberg AP, Meissner A, Vallot C, Ron G, Shema E.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis 1-3 . Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival 4-7 . Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

papers.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL.
papers.authors: Park J, Lynch LD, Blanco-Romero E, Masdemont-Maestro R, Méndez J, Chistol G.
papers.abstract: Eukaryotic genomes are exposed to numerous sources of DNA damage that impede replication. Only a decade ago, repriming by the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL was identified as a pathway that enables cells to tolerate DNA damage 1-4 . However, the molecular mechanism that underlies repriming remains poorly understood, and it is unclear how PRIMPOL is precisely targeted to stalled forks, where along single-stranded DNA PRIMPOL binds and how PRIMPOL is regulated to minimize error-prone DNA synthesis. Here, to dissect the molecular basis of repriming, we perform real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance. We directly visualize how stalled forks restart through repriming. We show that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG). This facilitates primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. At near-physiological concentrations, PRIMPOL reprimes leading strands in a CMG-dependent manner and polymerase ε extends those primers. This primary mode of repriming does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling. PRIMPOL overexpression and checkpoint activation promote a secondary mode of repriming, whereby PRIMPOL restarts DNA synthesis far from CMG and polymerase δ extends those primers. Our data reveal a simple yet effective mechanism that directs PRIMPOL's activity to stalled forks awaiting restart, and suggest a strategy to inhibit the repriming pathway.

papers.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis.
papers.authors: Song A, Wang Y, Wang G, Bae M, Wang Z, Gao G, Wu Z, Lu G, Meng J, Yu J, Park S, Garcia-Ocaña A, Fueger PT, Rao L, Frontini A, Liu Y, Jiang L, Zhu Y, Wang QA.
papers.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity 1-5 . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells) 6 . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal-immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

papers.title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses.
papers.authors: Yun JG, Kang H, Choi M, Lee K, Jeong Y, Choi J, Yi S, Kwak K, Rho J.
papers.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) displays, originating from early optical see-through head-mounted systems 1 , have evolved towards lightweight glasses that seamlessly integrate digital information with the physical world 2,3 . However, their widespread adoption requires compact optical systems that enable bright, wide-field and comfortable viewing. Diffractive waveguides (WGs) offer a promising approach towards lightweight AR displays yet face inherent trade-offs among field of view (FoV), optical efficiency and eyebox size owing to limited degrees of freedom in light control. Here we show an all-day-wearable AR glass prototype based on spatially varying, interwoven metasurfaces that provide several grating vectors for multidirectional light control. The resulting dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide (meta-WG) achieves a 30° FoV and an 8 × 8-mm 2 two-dimensional (2D) eyebox while maintaining an average luminance efficiency of 1,938 nits lm -1 (up to 4,225 nits lm -1 ) within a 1.5-mm-thick form factor. The prototype produces bright and stable virtual images under outdoor ambient illumination, demonstrating the compatibility of meta-WGs with practical wearable display requirements. By expanding the degrees of freedom for light routing beyond conventional diffractive WGs, our approach provides a scalable framework for balancing efficiency, viewing range and form factor, bringing high-performance AR glasses closer to practical consumer applications.

papers.title: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer's disease models.
papers.authors: Zhou H, Maynard JC, Pennacchio AJ, Apolonio A, Liu X, Yao L, Negahban M, Zhang Z, Ding B, Oberhauser J, Wen X, Yang MJ, Huang F, Chayama Y, Doddipalli S, Bernardi M, Domke L, Lo I, Simms J, Pan A, Du S, To NS, Wong PS, Duong D, Fox E, Seyfried NT, Cheung TH, Tracy TE, Burlingame AL, Yang AC.
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) has been defined primarily by what it excludes, yet the scale and function of physiological blood-to-brain protein transport remain largely unknown. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, we find that the healthy BBB samples 191 plasma proteins and permits 92 into the brain parenchyma. Enriched for carrier and metabolic functions, these proteins home to distinct brain cell types, such as apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) to astrocytes and alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) to microglia. This cell-type tropism relies on a BBB-parenchyma receptor hand-off: APOA1 crosses the BBB via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), a key Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity. Unlike LPS-induced nonspecific leakage, early-stage 5xFAD mice show selective BBB transport remodeling, with reduced APOA1 and increased SERPINA1 uptake. Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

papers.title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play.
papers.authors: Chen X, Tao X, Zhong Z, Zhu F, Zhang Y, Wang Y, Wang M, Li Y, Sun L, Ouyang Y, Ding Z, An M, Zhao Y, Zhou J, Zhang R, Xiong W, Ji N, Li Y.
papers.abstract: Juvenile social play is critical for neurodevelopment, yet the neural mechanisms organizing moment-to-moment interactions remain elusive. Using social behavior sequencing (Social-seq)-an occlusion-robust 3D pose estimation and unsupervised clustering pipeline-we found that nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine was tightly coupled to sub-second social syllables during naturalistic interactions. In wild-type juveniles, males exhibited a sharper dopaminergic contrast between proactive play and forced submission than females did, consistent with sex-divergent play strategies. In Shank3-deficient autism models, this process was fundamentally corrupted: proactive play-evoked dopamine responses were abolished in males and significantly sign-inverted in females, with male-specific enhancements during non-social behaviors, driving social play deficits. A multi-agent reinforcement learning model parameterized by disrupted, play-related dopaminergic reinforcement values recapitulated mutant phenotypes. Closed-loop optogenetic stimulation of ventral tegmental area (VTA)-NAc dopamine projections, time-locked to proactive play, restored reciprocal play in Shank3-deficient rats. Sub-second dopaminergic reinforcement thus orchestrates naturalistic social behavior, providing a behaviorally contingent interventional framework for neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection.
papers.authors: Matsushima Y, Durkee-Shock J, Alves DA, Nagata BM, Kim SA, Chan EC, Chaimongkol N, Ishiyama R, Barton K, Han A, Kelly LA, Ogbogu PU, Kumar S, Xu X, Briggs KC, Murakami K, Cohen JI, Keller MD, Sosnovtsev SV, Green KY.
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell-derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

papers.title: Reoperations After Lateral Rectus Resection/Plication Versus Medial Rectus Recession for Age-Related Distance Esotropia.
papers.authors: Parunakian E, Yehezkeli V, Velez FG, Meng Q, Douglas C, Demer JL.
papers.abstract: Introduction Medial rectus (MR) recession and lateral rectus (LR) resection/plication are common surgical approaches for age-related distance esotropia (ARDE), but relative advantages of the two approaches are unclear. This study evaluates their comparative efficacy, rate of reoperation, and time to reoperations. Study design Retrospective, comparative interventional case series. Methods Consecutive patients with ARDE undergoing strabismus surgery between 2014 and 2025 were reviewed. Outcomes Surgical alignment effect and time to recurrence and reoperation. Results The study included 86 patients (58 females, 28 males) of mean age 70.5±8.7 years (standard deviation). Median postoperative follow-up was 1.5 (Interquartile range, IQR: 0.6-3.1, range: 0.5-10.8) years, and 61% were followed for more than 1 year. There was no difference between MR recession and LR resection/plication in the 34-37% rate of interventions by spectacle prism or reoperation required for unsatisfactory surgical outcomes. The reduction in distance ET in the LR resection/plication group was 12.6±9.8 (range: -2 to 38) Δ, similar to the 9.1±7.3 (range: -6 to 25) Δ in the MR recession group (p=0.067). Both procedures demonstrated identical surgical dose responses of 2Δ/mm. There was an insignificant trend towards higher reoperation of 30% in the MR group than 23% in the LR group. Median time to reoperation was longer at 2.8 (IQR:1.8-6.4) years after MR recession than LR resection/plication at 0.7 (IQR: 0.7-1.2) years (p=0.001). Conclusion Both MR recession and LR resection/plication have similar early surgical effect and eventual rate of reoperation for recurrence of ARDE. Patients undergoing LR resection/plication require earlier reoperation.

papers.title: High-Dose Intravitreal Topotecan for Refractory or Recurrent Retinoblastoma: Efficacy, Safety and Intraocular Cytokine Profiles.
papers.authors: Lin X, Zheng Z, Chen H, Qian J, Liu Q, Ma R, Xue K.
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the outcomes and safety of high-dose intravitreal topotecan (100 μg, IVitT100) in the treatment of refractory or recurrent intraocular retinoblastoma (RB). Design Prospective, non-comparative case series. Participants 15 consecutive patients (15 eyes) with refractory or recurrent RB at the Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University between October 2023 and September 2025. Methods Participants received IVitT100 every four weeks. Clinical characteristics were recorded before and after treatment. Tumor control and injection-related complications were assessed at each visit. Aqueous humor cytokines and electroretinography (ERG) were analyzed to evaluate inflammatory changes and retinal function. Main outcome measures Treatment outcomes, including intraretinal tumor and intraocular seeds control, globe salvage rate, and ocular and systemic adverse events, were assessed during follow-up. Results At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6.0-14.0) after the final intravitreal injection, high-dose intravitreal topotecan achieved a globe salvage rate of 93%, with complete control of intraocular seeds in all eyes (100%) and complete regression of intraretinal tumors in 3 of 4 eyes (75%). Baseline ERG amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.5-14.7), post-treatment amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.9-15.8), showing no significant retinal function impairment (P = 0.429). None of the 27 cytokines showed significant changes between pre- and post-treatment measurements in RB eyes (all P > 0.05). No severe ocular or systemic adverse events were reported. Conclusions IVitT100 is highly effective for refractory or recurrent RB with vitreous seeds, subretinal seeds, and intraretinal tumors. It exhibits minimal retinal toxicity and does not induce intraocular inflammatory responses, supporting its role as a safe and effective first-line intravitreal therapy for advanced RB.

papers.title: Precursor lesions are associated with distinct growth kinetics after atrophy onset.
papers.authors: Gagliardi OM, Doshi U, Amin R, Peña DF, Jiang J, Gregori G, Sahoo NK, Hasan N, Iannetta D, Chhablani J.
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether atrophic lesions arising from different retinal precursors show distinct temporal growth kinetics in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Design Retrospective longitudinal cohort study. Participants 109 eyes of 88 patients with intermediate AMD (iAMD) developing cRORA. Methods Consecutive eyes with iAMD progressing to complete retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (cRORA) were identified by retrospective back-tracking of serial spectral-domain OCT. Precursors, defined as lesions that progressed to cRORA at the site of onset, were classified as drusenoid, subretinal drusenoid deposit (SDD), or acquired vitelliform lesion (AVL). Atrophy was segmented automatically on en face projections and manually corrected when needed. Temporal kinetics during the first 3 years after cRORA onset were assessed using piecewise linear time with knots at 1 and 2 years, adjusting for atrophic area, eccentricity, and number of foci at onset. Main outcome measures Rate and temporal kinetics of square-root-transformed total atrophic area growth by precursor. Results Of 109 eyes progressing to cRORA, 66 arose from drusenoid, 31 from SDD, and 12 from AVL. After cRORA, the model-estimated growth rate was different according to the precursor lesions, with 0.197 mm/year in the drusenoid group, 0.383 mm/year in the SDD group, and 0.429 mm/year in the AVL group (P Conclusion The study finds distinct temporal trajectories: atrophy arising from drusenoid lesions grows more steadily, whereas from SDD accelerates later, and from AVL grows rapidly early then decelerates. SDD presence elsewhere may be less important than whether the atrophy arose from SDD. The findings may have prognostic implications, representing a stratification variable in clinical trials.

papers.title: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis.
papers.authors: Zeng W, Lamelas L, Scaramozzino D, Chen ZA, Rappsilber J, Xue S, Jaeger KE, Orellana L, Sampathkumar A, Wigge PA.
papers.abstract: Temperature is molecular motion, but how living systems sense this is poorly understood. Many responses in plants integrate light and temperature signals, for example, via light receptors and the circadian clock. CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1) regulates light signaling and is necessary for responding to temperature. We show that COP1 acts as a temperature-dependent switch, becoming activated by a warm temperature-induced conformational change. An intramolecular Val-Pro (VP) motif binds to the active site of COP1 at low temperatures, preventing substrate docking. At warmer temperatures, the VP motif becomes detached, enabling client proteins to bind and be degraded. This discovery explains how plants are able to obtain a precise readout of temperature within a given climate range. Altering the binding of the VP motif is sufficient to adjust the temperature range within which the plant responds. This helps us understand how plants are able to adapt to different climates.

papers.title: Nicotianamine-driven nickel transport to sink organs underpins maize productivity.
papers.authors: Chao ZF, Chen Y, Wu JC, Wang YL, Xiao Y, Peng Y, Fan LY, Wang X, Han ML, Liu HJ, von Wirén N, Yan J, Chao DY.
papers.abstract: Nickel (Ni), the last essential trace element identified in plants, has long been enigmatic regarding the genetic basis underlying its homeostasis and its agricultural significance. Using genome-wide association analysis, we identified ZmNAET1 as a key transporter controlling Ni allocation to seeds. Mechanistically, ZmNAET1 mediates nicotianamine secretion and enables nicotianamine-dependent phloem loading of Ni in nodes and subsequent Ni translocation into sink organs. Mutants lacking ZmNAET1 exhibit significant yield penalties, decreased seed germination velocity, and drastically shortened seed longevity. In an irreplaceable role, supplemented Ni fully rescued seed germination and proper vegetative development of the mutants. We show that NAET1-dependent delivery of Ni to urease is essential for amino acid turnover in developing sink organs, revealing an unappreciated role of Ni in yield formation of graminaceous plants. This study uncovers an underestimated requirement for nicotianamine and Ni and opens a new research avenue toward optimizing micronutrient provision for cereal crop productivity.

papers.title: In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Yang E, Aceves-Salvador J, Castrillon C, Herrmann US, Akama-Garren EH, Carroll MC, Moffitt JR.
papers.abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions.

papers.title: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping.
papers.authors: Zhang ZE, Kim A, Suboc N, Mancuso N, Gazal S.
papers.abstract: Population-scale single-cell RNA sequencing enables mapping genetic effects on gene regulation at the cellular level (for example, single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs)). However, existing sc-eQTL mapping approaches are either not designed for analyzing sparse counts in single-cell RNA sequencing data or become computationally intractable at scale. Here we developed jaxQTL-an efficient pseudobulk sc-eQTL mapping framework using highly efficient count-based models. In simulations, we demonstrated that jaxQTL with a negative binomial model provides calibrated inference while outperforming linear models. In OneK1K data, jaxQTL identified 16% more eGenes than linear models, while running substantially faster than single-cell Poisson mixed effect models. We found that fine-mapped sc-eQTLs are more distal from transcription starting site than those identified in all cells (bulk-eQTLs; P = 1 × 10 -4 ) and more enriched in cell-type-specific enhancers (P = 3 × 10 -10 ), revealing distal regulatory effects that are missed in bulk tissues. Although sc-eQTLs are largely shared across cell types, cell-type-specificity increases with distance to transcription starting site. Finally, sc-eQTLs explain a greater proportion of single nucleotide polymorphism-heritability than bulk-eQTLs across 16 blood and immune-related traits (9.90 ± 0.88% versus 6.10 ± 0.76%) and prioritize disease-associated genes missed by the bulk approach (such as IL6ST), improving, but not closing, the missing link between genome-wide association studies and eQTLs.

papers.title: Intravenous pulse methylprednisolone versus placebo for ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy (EtON): A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.
papers.authors: Takkar A, Kaur P, Vinay Mahesh K, Tigari B, Muthu V, Soundappan K, Chaurasia S, Singh R, Sukhija J, Singh P, Malhotra S, Lal V.
papers.abstract: Purpose Ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy (EtON) is a dose-dependent adverse drug effect that may cause irreversible visual impairment, with no established therapeutic interventions beyond drug cessation. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of high-dose, short-term intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP) among patients with EtON. Design This was a prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial (RCT) conducted at a tertiary care center in India (March 2021 to August 2024). Subjects, participants, and/or controls Patients reporting visual loss while receiving ethambutol and diagnosed with EtON using a pre-defined diagnostic criteria were enrolled. Methods, intervention, or testing A total of 100 patients with EtON were randomized (1:1) using block randomization. Participants received either high-dose IVMP (1gram per day for 5 days) or placebo, alongside standard-of-care therapy. Main outcome measures The primary endpoint was two or more lines improvement in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) on Snellen's chart (equivalent to at least ten letters on the logMAR) at 6 months. Secondary endpoints included improvement in mean deviation (MD) and visual field index (VFI) on automated perimetry, along with safety, and adjusted treatment effects. Results At 6 months, 36 (72.0%) patients in the IVMP arm versus 23 (46.0%) in the placebo arm achieved an improvement of two or more lines in BCVA (p=0.008). However, the between-group difference in mean final BCVA was not statistically significant (0.54 (0.6) vs 0.61 (0.6), p=0.534). Significant improvement in visual field parameters was noted in IVMP arm: mean MD (-9.40 vs -13.99 (mean difference: 4.59, 95% CI: 1.35-7.83)) and mean VFI (71.27 vs 62.35 (mean difference: 8.92; 95% CI: 0.20-17.65)). Adjusted analysis confirmed improvement in visual outcomes with IVMP (adjusted risk ratio: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.14, 2.29), consistent across subgroups. No serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. Conclusions Short-term high-dose IVMP administration was associated with a greater proportion of BCVA responders and better visual field parameters in patients with EtON. This is the first RCT to evaluate the role of corticosteroids in EtON. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger trials.

papers.title: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings.
papers.authors: Jiang L, Tan ZC, Grabski IN, Hao Y, Nakatsuka N, Sarkar S, Shenoy A, Satija R.
papers.abstract: Single-cell genomics is transformative for characterizing cellular heterogeneity, but many biological questions require comparing samples rather than individual cells. Typical analyses compare "case" and "control" groups, ignoring sample-level variation within them. Here, we present scSLIDE (single-cell sample-level inference using density estimation), a framework that transforms each sample's single-cell data into a compact profile describing where its cells are distributed in high-dimensional space. By comparing these density profiles, scSLIDE calculates embeddings to characterize variation across samples. We implement scSLIDE in version 6 of our Seurat package and apply it to COVID-19 infection, Alzheimer's disease, and zebrafish embryogenesis. scSLIDE reveals patient subgroups, reconstructs disease trajectories, and identifies coordinated cellular programs across samples. We discover separable axes of infection and severity, a trajectory of Alzheimer's progression, and embryonic "pseudostages" that vary across and within time points. Our results demonstrate how case-control analyses collapse rich biological variation into binary labels and how sample-level embedding represents a powerful analytical alternative.

papers.title: Deciphering the gene-centric spatial dynamics across tissue and time with GeneSPOT.
papers.authors: Zou Q, Wang Z, Li S, Lin S, Han C, Cui Y, Li S, Wang L, Zhang D, Zhang W, Qian BZ, Gao R, Yuan Z.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide unprecedented opportunities to investigate how molecular programs are organized within tissues. However, existing analytical frameworks primarily focus on identifying cellular states and characterizing differentially expressed molecular features across these states. The relational spatial organization of molecular features and its dynamics across biological contexts therefore remain largely unexplored. Here we present Gene SPatial Optimal Transport (GeneSPOT), a gene-centric computational framework for characterizing the spatial relationships among genes and quantifying their reorganization across biological conditions. Although gene-centric in design, GeneSPOT generalizes to other molecular features. Across diverse applications, GeneSPOT resolved tissue structures, integrated paired and unpaired spatial multi-omics data, unveiled the spatial convergence of gene programs during embryonic development and identified aging-associated spatial reorganization among genes whose expression did not change significantly with age. GeneSPOT thus complements conventional cell-centric analysis, providing a framework for deciphering how spatial relationships among molecular features are reorganized across biological conditions and over time.

papers.title: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Madduri AV, Ellis RJ, Lakhani CM, Bennett DA, Patel CJ.
papers.abstract: Univariate differential expression analysis dominates single-cell transcriptomic studies of Alzheimer's disease, yet marginal testing alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure or distinguish clinical from neuropathological signatures. Here we introduce TriSCOPE, a framework integrating multivariate predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression, and pseudotime inference, applied to six Alzheimer's disease snRNA-seq datasets comprising ~4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors. Across six major brain cell types and 41 subclusters, we identify cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that are largely non-overlapping with differentially expressed genes, revealing disease-relevant signals invisible to univariate approaches. Conditional GWAS-eQTL colocalization anchors a subset of these predictively expressed genes to inherited Alzheimer's disease risk loci, including 27 genetically supported gene-cell type pairs (among them ARL17B, JAZF1) with no significant differential expression. Integration across all three analytical branches nominates high-confidence convergent programs including astrocytic stress markers (such as GFAP, MT2A), neuronal signaling genes (like RASGEF1B, LINGO1, NRG1), and microglial and oligodendrocyte regulators (including SYTL3, SPP1, APOD). Comparison of clinical and neuropathological models reveals cell-type-specific divergence between cognitive and pathological Alzheimer's disease signatures. Key predictively expressed genes including ARL17B, LINGO1, and APOE replicate across independent cohorts, with cross-cohort generalizability confirmed across all three analytical branches of TriSCOPE.
